title: Specialized HF and VHF antennas
blurb: Choose antennas for NVIS, multiband, receive-only and loop uses, and explain traps, stacking, log-periodics and end-fed feeds.

G9D01.why: NVIS needs energy sent nearly straight up: a **horizontal dipole 1/10 to 1/4 λ high** does that. At ½ λ it has a null overhead.
G9D01.trap: A vertical radiates little straight up.

G9D02.why: At the end of a half wave the voltage is highest and current lowest, so impedance is **very high**.
G9D02.trap: The low impedance (about 73 Ω) is at the center, not the end.

G9D03.why: A halo is a loop lying flat, so it radiates equally in every direction **in the plane of the halo**.

G9D04.why: Traps isolate sections of wire at different frequencies, which **enables multiband operation**.
G9D04.trap: Traps don't notch spurs or limit operation to one band.

G9D05.why: Stacked Yagis add gain by **narrowing the main lobe in elevation**. The azimuth width stays the same.

G9D06.why: A log-periodic works over a **wide bandwidth** because a different part of it is active on each frequency.
G9D06.trap: It does not beat a Yagi in gain per element.

G9D07.why: **Element length and spacing vary logarithmically** along the boom: each is a fixed ratio from the next.

G9D08.why: A motor changes how much of the coil is in the circuit: it varies the **base loading inductance**.

G9D09.why: A Beverage is a long, low, terminated wire for **directional receiving** on MF and low HF.
G9D09.trap: It is a receiving antenna, not for transmitting.

G9D10.why: A small loop is strongest in its own plane and has nulls **broadside to the loop**.
G9D10.trap: Nulls are not in the plane of the loop.

G9D11.why: Multiband antennas resonate on several frequencies, so they have **poor harmonic rejection**.
G9D11.trap: A tuner or open-wire line isn't required.

G9D12.why: A dipole with a single central support, ends drooping, is an **inverted V**.
G9D12.trap: A sloper hangs from one end.
